Aristotle Onassis, one of the richest men who ever lived, had one rule for when he was broke: go get in the room with people who have more money than you.

He'd study how they thought and acted, and mimic it, on purpose.

Kevin Trudeau's version of the same rule: your income is always the average of your five best friends. Your parents were right when they told you to stop hanging around certain people - it works the same way in reverse, with the right crowd.

Who are your five? And what are they averaging you toward?

Arnold Schwarzenegger used the same move twice, in two completely different industries.

To become a bodybuilding champion, he trained with the champions - not just their workouts, their whole mindset, how they thought and talked.

Most people don't know his second career was real estate. He did the exact same thing: joined the right rooms, associated with wealthy developers who knew more than he did, and became one of the biggest real estate players in Beverly Hills.

It wasn't talent that repeated. It was the method.
